name: regenerate
title: Regenerate minutes
description: Bring a meeting's minutes up to date as a background job (kind `regenerate`). Preprocessing, transcription and diarization run idempotently first: each is skipped when its recorded input hashes and parameters are unchanged and only runs when it never ran (a meeting stopped with auto_process=false, a process job that failed) or when set_meeting_config changed its parameters (transcription_engine, transcription_model, diarization_engine, language, vocab_hints). Then alignment → LLM integration → minutes generation run with the same idempotency: a new minutes version is appended only when something changed — existing versions are never overwritten. An explicit minutes_model applies only to text minutes and is part of the generation cache key, including its provider, connection ID/revision, model ID, parameters and cache_epoch. Unchanged inputs and selection reuse the existing version. Changing only this selection does not rerun transcription or LLM integration and never silently substitutes a provider or model. Use it after set_meeting_config or register_context, to process a meeting stopped with auto_process=false, or to retry a failed process job. When minutes_model, minutes_ensemble and transcription_model are all null, `force=true` re-runs alignment, integration and generation even when their inputs are unchanged (still appending a new version); preprocessing and transcription are never forced. When minutes_model, minutes_ensemble or transcription_model is selected, `force=true` is rejected with invalid_argument. To explicitly start a new selected-model attempt, confirm retransmission with the user, save an incremented minutes_model.cache_epoch through set_meeting_config, and call regenerate with the returned config as expected_config, a new request_id and force=false. A previous unknown selected-model generation outcome is never automatically resent; ordinary regeneration with the same selection cannot bypass its receipt. `reason` is recorded in manifest.regenerations. `scope` is the scope selector (default deny: a scoped meeting needs its scope in the request). When the saved minutes_model, minutes_ensemble or transcription_model is non-null, expected_config is required and must be the full effective config confirmed by the caller. Any supplied expected_config is compared with the current config under the meeting lock before changes or job creation; a mismatch returns configuration_conflict without sending or generating. `request_id` is the client-generated idempotency key: repeating the call returns the same job_id. On failure returns an error_envelope (isError=true) with code: not_found (unknown meeting), scope_denied (the request does not cover the meeting's scope), busy (the meeting is still recording, or a job is already queued / running for it), policy_violation (the configured transcription_model, minutes_model, llm_provider or engines are not allowed by external_send_policy — nothing is silently downgraded), engine_unavailable (configured engine / provider not installed), configuration_conflict, authentication_required, model_unavailable, invalid_argument, internal. Failures inside the job are reported by get_job_status. API transcription reuses verified successful chunks regardless of cache_epoch; changing only the epoch does not replace completed transcripts or change downstream fingerprints. Audio is split deterministically into nonoverlapping chunks of at most 9600000 samples at 16000 Hz, processed sequentially mic then system, at most 144 chunks and 24 total audio hours. A transcription_retry is one explicit user confirmation to retransmit a single outcome-unknown chunk, not a saved setting. It requires expected_config with a non-null transcription_model, force=false and selected cache_epoch greater than blocked_epoch. Before any ASR send, compare the full config, actual input/chunk fingerprints and latest blocked epoch; reject mismatch without sending. Persist the new pending epoch before sending, consume that confirmation once, reuse successes and never implicitly retry other unknown chunks. Retry, restart, elapsed time, selection clear/restore and ordinary epoch changes do not erase unknown outcomes. Confirmation details come from get_job_status.error.details with reason=transcription_outcome_unknown. Initial API transcription sends no vocabulary prompt or speaker reference audio. Cancellation after sending cannot guarantee provider-side processing or billing has stopped. minutes_retry confirms one outcome-unknown ensemble call and is mutually exclusive with transcription_retry. Its run_id/node_id/call_id identify the currently inspected confirmation target; blocked_attempt_id supplies historical origin, which read/error provenance exposes separately. Require the full expected_config and its non-null minutes_ensemble, reject force=true, compare the target and latest unknown receipt, and consume confirmation once with the new pending attempt before sending. Other unknown calls remain blocked. Changing epoch, run or generator identity alone is never a retry confirmation. Normal resume reuses validated successful nodes and processes only known unfinished dependencies. Generation runs sequentially with a cumulative maximum of 64 attempts per run; reused successes do not consume new attempts. Publish a final minutes version only after all required drafts, synthesis and evidence validation succeed. Keep partial successful artifacts readable and retain the previous final version on failure. Same-request-id recovery requires an identical request body; do not automatically resend an ambiguously accepted request. One content-unknown retry ancestry is limited to 64 lifetime attempts including its origin, independently of each run's 64-attempt budget. Attempt 65 is rejected before consuming the minutes_retry proof, reserving run budget or sending; the existing unknown and chain remain unchanged, and the safe node error reason is minutes_retry_limit_exceeded. This lifetime limit does not consume the budget of another content identity. Ensemble synthesis-leaf execution is packet-local. For each packet, canonical candidate claim/question units (or one empty sentinel) are partitioned deterministically by fixed unit and character limits. Each stable occurrence is one leaf whose current inputs are exactly the packet source plus the unique draft_chunk artifacts contributing its units; the same source/draft_chunk pair may repeat when one document spans occurrences. Its wire request may also include fixed synthesis instructions/common brief, and its request hash and content fingerprint bind that request and selected model content conditions. Aggregate drafts and other packets are absent. Stable packet/candidate projections, duplicate and partition ordinals/hashes and unit order preserve leaf identity and downstream aggregation order when an unrelated packet changes. Publication uses a side-effect-free preflight to freeze the exact multi-root proof made from every preflight-time canonical draft root and the final synthesis root. Before coverage comparison, each canonical draft pair and each leaf artifact's immutable direct input IDs are normalized through that binding's frozen direct dependency mappings to effective current-run IDs, using identity mapping for unchanged IDs. Every mapped ID must be an exact frozen member/adoption under the frozen authorization and projection; content equality alone cannot substitute another artifact. All leaf wire occurrences must then be the exact disjoint union of every normalized canonical draft's partitioned units/sentinel, with no omission, duplicate or extra unit, and each leaf's normalized inputs must exactly match its contributing packet source/draft_chunks. Every validated nonempty leaf must reach the final effective closure; only a validated empty leaf may remain outside. One exclusive meeting/configuration/provider fence covers preflight, durable manifest write, acknowledgement and publication-sensitive reads. It prevents cancellation or run, authorization, membership or dependency change from interleaving. A read waits for acknowledgement or performs exact stopped-publication reconciliation under the fence. If execution stops after manifest publication but before acknowledgement, recovery first verifies the exact same candidate/version and completes acknowledgement without a provider resend or different publication; mismatch is an internal error. Acknowledgement revalidates and saves the same frozen proof, public provenance and version as an immutable store publication record. Past provenance is read from this record and never rebuilt from later display rebinding.

expected_config.description: Full effective config confirmed by the caller, as returned by get_meeting. Required when saved minutes_model, minutes_ensemble or transcription_model is non-null, and always with transcription_retry or minutes_retry. Compare under the meeting lock before enqueueing; mismatch returns configuration_conflict without sending. Omission for legacy state is decided by the server.

force.description: Default false. Only when minutes_model, minutes_ensemble and transcription_model are all null may true re-run stages from alignment. API transcription and selected minutes models reject true. For an unknown ASR chunk, both a higher transcription cache_epoch and matching one-chunk transcription_retry confirmation are required; successful chunks are never forced. Ensemble generation always rejects true; unknown-call retransmission uses only a matching minutes_retry confirmation.

reason.description: Free-text reason recorded in manifest.regenerations (e.g. "added Notion transcript").

job_id.description: The enqueued regenerate job; poll with get_job_status.
